Flow Work: Processes asset request approvals, updates approval status, and notifies the requester.
Details Explain working: 1.Trigger: The flow starts when a new item is created in your SharePoint list. 2.Team Members: It lists team members and processes the item data. 3.Teams Groups: Retrieves Teams group configurations and filters for admin and user groups. 4.User Profile: Gets the profile of the item’s author. 5.Adaptive Card: Posts an approval card in Teams for action (Approve/Reject). 6.Approval Logic: Based on the response, updates the item status and notifies users in Teams.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated)

1. Trigger
SharePoint connector, "When an item is created". The flow instance starts only for a new list item. That item is the asset request record for the rest of the run.

2. Team members
The flow lists team members and processes the new item data. This builds the people context used later for the approval card and notifications.

3. Teams groups
It retrieves the Teams group configuration and filters that configuration to the admin group and the user group. Only those two filtered groups are used downstream.

4. User profile
It gets the profile of the item author. The author is the requester whose profile is used when the approval is posted and when users are notified.

5. Adaptive card
It posts an approval adaptive card in Microsoft Teams. The card actions exposed to the approver are Approve and Reject.

6. Approval logic
The flow waits on the card response, then branches on that response:
- It updates the SharePoint item approval status to match Approve or Reject.
- It notifies users in Teams of the outcome.

Result
The asset request item status is updated and the requester side is notified in Teams. No schedule is involved; each new item is one run.

Flow Work: Automatically adds a new user to a meeting and sends the required notifications.
Details Explain working: 1.Trigger: Starts when a SharePoint item is created or modified and has participants. 2.Initialize Variables: Sets up arrays for old/new participants and other helper variables. 3.Fetch Changes: Gets the latest and previous versions of the item to compare participant lists. 4.Compare Participants: Identifies new participants by comparing old and new lists. 5.User Lookup: Retrieves user details from another SharePoint list. 6.Teams Notification: Posts adaptive cards in Teams chats/channels to alert about meetings. 7.Update Records: Updates SharePoint with meeting and time details.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated)

1. Trigger
SharePoint "When an item is created or modified", with a participant condition. A run starts only when the meeting item has participants.

2. Initialize variables
Arrays are initialized for the old participant list and the new participant list, plus helper variables used while the two lists are compared.

3. Fetch changes
The flow reads the latest version and the previous version of the same SharePoint item. Those two versions are the inputs for the participant diff.

4. Compare participants
Old and new participant lists are compared. The difference is the set of newly added participants. Existing participants are not treated as new.

5. User lookup
For the new participants, user details are read from a second SharePoint list.

6. Teams notification
Adaptive cards are posted in Teams chats or channels to alert those users about the meeting.

7. Update records
The SharePoint meeting item is updated with the meeting details and the time details after the participant change is processed.

Result
A created or modified meeting item that gained participants produces a user lookup, a Teams alert, and an updated SharePoint meeting/time record.

Flow Work: Generates HHHH employee attendance details in table format and identifies employees who are on leave.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: The flow starts on a daily schedule (recurrence) at 12 PM India Standard Time.
Main Purpose: It generates an attendance report for the HHHH team, including leave and availability details for various teams and employees.
Data Sources: It pulls data from SharePoint lists (Leave Request, Contacts, Employees).
Processing: The flow filters, matches, and counts employees, calculates leave statistics, and builds an HTML report.
Output: The report is posted in a Microsoft Teams group chat.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Scheduled)

1. Trigger
Recurrence daily at 12:00 PM India Standard Time. One run covers the HHHH attendance report for that day.

2. Data sources
Three SharePoint lists are read:
- Leave Request
- Contacts
- Employees

3. Processing
The flow filters the retrieved rows, matches employees across the lists, and counts them. Leave statistics are calculated from the matched Leave Request data. Availability is derived for the teams and employees included in the report.

4. Report build
The matched counts, leave statistics, and availability details are rendered as an HTML report in table form.

5. Output
The HTML report is posted to a Microsoft Teams group chat.

Result
The HHHH group chat receives the daily attendance table, including who is on leave and who is available. The flow does not update the Leave Request or Employees lists; it reads them and publishes the report.

Flow Work: Generates a report of employees who logged in late.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: The flow starts daily at 12:01 PM IST.
SharePoint Data: It retrieves employee attendance data from SharePoint.
Processing: Filters employees who spent more time and those with late logins.
Variables: Stores day, date, and late login counts.
Reporting: Builds a late login report table.
Notification: Posts the report in a Teams group chat, except on weekends.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Scheduled)

1. Trigger
Recurrence daily at 12:01 PM IST.

2. SharePoint read
Employee attendance rows are retrieved from SharePoint. This is the only data source described for the report.

3. Filter
Two subsets are produced from that attendance data:
- employees who spent more time
- employees with late logins

4. Variables
Day, date, and the late-login counts are stored in variables and used as the report header and totals.

5. Report table
A late-login report table is built from the filtered rows and the count variables.

6. Notification rule
The table is posted to a Teams group chat. The post is skipped on weekends.

Result
On a weekday the Teams group chat gets the late-login table with day, date, and counts. On Saturday and Sunday the flow does not post.

Flow Work: Sends automated meeting reminder notifications.
Details Explain working:
1.Trigger: Runs daily at 10:10 AM IST. 2.Get_items: Retrieves meeting data from SharePoint for the current day. 3.Apply_to_each: Processes each meeting item:

Extracts participants.
Filters relevant Teams groups.
For each group member, checks if they are a participant.
Posts an adaptive card in Teams group chat with meeting details. 4.Handles participant lists: Formats and displays participant names. 5.Manages meeting info: Shows/hides details and provides links to join or view meetings.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Scheduled)

1. Trigger
Recurrence daily at 10:10 AM IST.

2. Get_items
Meeting items for the current day are read from SharePoint. Only that day's meetings enter the loop.

3. Apply to each meeting
For every meeting item the flow:
- extracts the participant list
- filters the Teams groups that are relevant to that meeting
- for each member of those groups, checks whether that member is a participant
- posts an adaptive card in the Teams group chat with the meeting details

4. Participant list handling
Participant names are formatted and displayed on the card.

5. Meeting info handling
The card shows or hides meeting details and includes links to join the meeting or to view the meeting.

Result
Each current-day meeting produces a Teams reminder card for the participants found inside the filtered groups, with join and view links.

Flow Work: Generates a daily report showing employees who are on leave.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: The flow starts daily at 1 PM IST.
Employee Data: It initializes variables and fetches employee and leave data from SharePoint.
Processing: It matches leave requests with employee details, filters for today’s leaves, and prepares a formatted HTML table.
Condition: If it’s a weekday and there are leaves, it posts the leave report to a Teams group chat.
Output: If no leaves, it shows a “No leaves today” message.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Scheduled)

1. Trigger
Recurrence daily at 1:00 PM IST.

2. Employee and leave data
Variables are initialized. Employee data and leave data are then fetched from SharePoint.

3. Match and filter
Each leave request is matched to an employee record. The matched set is filtered to leaves that apply today. Other dates are dropped before the table is built.

4. HTML table
The remaining rows are formatted into an HTML table.

5. Post condition
The table is posted to a Teams group chat only when both are true:
- the day is a weekday
- at least one leave remains after the filter

6. Empty result
When there are no leaves, the output message is "No leaves today".

Result
Weekday Teams chat shows either the today's-leave table or the no-leaves message. The flow reads leave and employee data; it does not approve or reject the leave request.

Actions:

Uses Microsoft Graph API to fetch chat groups.

Loops through each group to list members.
Stores group details and members in an array.
Updates or creates a SharePoint item with group configurations.

Recurrence twice a day, at 11:00 IST and 15:00 IST.

Flow Work: Automatically generates and processes the client leave report, including employee leave details and leave status.
Details Explain working: Compose: Takes the trigger body and prepares it for further actions. 2.Parse_JSON: Runs after Compose, extracting "html", "reportPreset", and "generatedAt" from the composed data. 3.Initialize_variable: Runs after Parse_JSON, initializing a string variable called "leaveRows". 4.Post_message_in_a_chat_or_channel: Runs after Initialize_variable, posting a message to a Microsoft Teams group chat using the parsed HTML content.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated)

Action order is fixed by run-after dependencies.

1. Compose
The trigger body is taken as-is and prepared for the following actions. The report HTML is expected to already be inside that body. This flow does not query the Leave Request list in the documented steps.

2. Parse JSON
Runs after Compose. Three properties are extracted:
- html — the report markup
- reportPreset — the preset that produced the report
- generatedAt — the generation timestamp

Runs after Parse JSON. A string variable named leaveRows is initialized.

4. Post message in a chat or channel

The client leave report, including employee leave details and leave status carried in html, is published to the Teams group chat. leaveRows is initialized in this path; the posted content is the parsed html.

Flow Work: Synchronizes Parent SP PXC Family information.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: The flow starts when an item is created or modified in your SharePoint list, filtered by specific conditions (PercentComplete between 0.05 and 0.9, TaskType is 'Task').
Main Actions: It checks for changes, gathers related project, sprint, and cycle data, and builds arrays for processing.
Processing: The flow loops through tasks and projects, updates items based on their status, and manages variables for tracking progress.
Purpose: It automates task and project updates, ensuring data consistency and workflow efficiency.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated)

1. Trigger
SharePoint "When an item is created or modified", with a trigger filter:
- PercentComplete is between 0.05 and 0.9
- TaskType is 'Task'
Items outside that range or with a different task type do not start the flow.

2. Change check and related data
The flow checks what changed on the item, then gathers the related project, sprint, and cycle data. Those related records are placed into arrays for processing.

3. Loop
The flow loops tasks and projects. Inside the loop, items are updated according to their status. Variables are updated to track progress as each item is processed.

Result
Parent SP PXC Family task and project records stay consistent: only in-progress Task items (5% to 90% complete) cause related project, sprint, and cycle data to be recalculated and written back.

Flow Name: All Task List- Child Scalablel Project Family 2

At the end, the flow sends a response with the updated arrays and project details.

Technical runtime path (Instant / manual)

Manual button. The flow receives the task and project payload for Child Scalable Project Family 2.

2. Compose and Initialize variable

3. Type and status conditions
Conditions classify the item as Project, Sprint, Cycle, or Workstream, and also check the task completion status. Each branch decides whether that item is queried further.

Flow Work: Processes OMT questions and rejection requests and updates the related workflow status.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: The flow starts manually via an HTTP request.
User & Task Initialization: It initializes variables for users and tasks.
Task Binding: Tasks are processed and formatted into a table.
Teams Group Retrieval: It fetches Teams group configurations from SharePoint.
Group Filtering: Filters for the "OMT Notifications group."
Group Processing: For each group, it processes members, filters users, and posts adaptive cards to Teams group chats.
Condition Check: If no group exists, it creates a new Teams group and posts a card.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated, HTTP start)

1. Trigger
HTTP request. The body carries the OMT question or rejection request.

2. User and task initialization
Variables for users and for tasks are initialized before any Teams post.

3. Task binding
The tasks in the request are processed and formatted into a table. That table is the content later shown on the adaptive card.

4. Teams group retrieval
Teams group configuration is read from SharePoint.

5. Group filter
The configuration is filtered to the group named "OMT Notifications group".

6. Group processing
For each matching group, the flow processes members, filters the users, and posts adaptive cards to the Teams group chats.

7. Missing-group branch
If no matching group exists, the flow creates a new Teams group and posts the card there.

Result
The OMT question or rejection is turned into a task table, delivered as an adaptive card to the OMT Notifications group, and the related workflow status is updated. If the group is missing, it is created in the same run.

Flow Work: Runs scheduled task actions and processes pending task operations.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: The flow starts on a daily recurrence (every day at 1:10 AM GMT).
Data Preparation: It calculates the current and tomorrow’s date, and sets up the SharePoint list name.
Get Data: Retrieves items from the SharePoint "Task Actions" list filtered by date and action type.
Process Data: For each item:
Checks if the task date matches today.
Gets Teams group info and filters for the "Task Actions" group.
For each group member, checks if their email matches the tagged user.
If yes, posts a Teams message, updates a variable, fetches task details, and deletes the item from SharePoint.
If no group exists, creates a new Teams group, posts a message, fetches task details, and deletes the item.
Variables: Uses variables to track if a group exists.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Scheduled)

1. Trigger
Recurrence every day at 1:10 AM GMT.

2. Data preparation
The flow calculates today's date and tomorrow's date, and sets the SharePoint list name used for the rest of the run.

3. Get data
Items are read from the SharePoint list "Task Actions", filtered by date and by action type.

4. Per item
Apply to each Task Actions item:
- Compare the task date with today. Only today's items continue.
- Read Teams group info and filter to the group named "Task Actions".
- For each member of that group, compare the member email with the tagged user on the item.
- If the email matches: post a Teams message, update the tracking variable, fetch the task details, and delete the Task Actions item from SharePoint.
- If no Task Actions group exists: create a new Teams group, post the message, fetch the task details, and delete the SharePoint item.

5. Group-exists variable
A variable records whether the Task Actions group was found, and that flag selects the post path versus the create-group path.

Result
Pending Task Actions due today are delivered to the tagged user in Teams and then removed from the Task Actions list so the same item is not processed again.

Flow Work: Generates a report for employees with short login hours.
Details Explain working:
The flow is triggered daily at 12:00 PM IST.
It retrieves items from a SharePoint list, filtering by date.
Data is transformed and filtered to identify employees with short login hours and late logins.
Two HTML tables are built: one for login hour shortages and one for late logins.
If there’s no data, a “No data available for today” row is added.
On weekdays, the tables are posted to a Microsoft Teams group chat.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Scheduled)

1. Trigger
Recurrence daily at 12:00 PM IST.

2. Get items
SharePoint list items are retrieved with a date filter so the run is limited to the current report date.

3. Transform and filter
The rows are transformed, then split into:
- employees with short login hours
- employees with late logins

4. Two HTML tables
One HTML table is built for login-hour shortages. A second HTML table is built for late logins.

5. Empty-table rule
If either set has no rows, a row with the text "No data available for today" is added to that table.

6. Weekday post
Both tables are posted to a Microsoft Teams group chat only on weekdays.

Result
On a weekday the Teams chat receives the short-hours table and the late-login table. An empty category still posts a table that contains the no-data row.

Flow Name: HHHH Meeting flows create task with time entry
Flow Work: Automatically creates HHHH tasks from meeting information and records the associated time entry.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: Runs every 5 minutes when a new item is created in your SharePoint list.
Initialization: Sets up variables for users, time tracking, and arrays.
Processing:
Retrieves teams/groups and user details.
Creates and updates SharePoint items for meetings and tasks.
Filters participants and handles group membership.
Notifications: Posts adaptive cards to Microsoft Teams chats/channels for meeting alerts.
Conditions & Loops: Uses conditions and loops to process participants, update time entries, and manage group notifications.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated)

1. Trigger
SharePoint "When a new item is created". The trigger is configured to check every 5 minutes, so a new meeting item is picked up on that polling interval.

2. Initialization
Variables are set for users, for time tracking, and for the arrays used while participants and groups are processed.

3. Processing
- Teams/groups and user details are retrieved.
- SharePoint items are created and updated for the meeting and for the task.
- Participants are filtered and group membership is handled.

4. Notifications
Adaptive cards are posted to Microsoft Teams chats or channels as the meeting alert.

5. Conditions and loops
Conditions and Apply to each loops walk the participants, update the time entries, and send the group notifications.

Result
A new HHHH meeting item becomes a SharePoint task plus a time entry, and the participants are notified in Teams.

Flow Work: Runs the scheduled WT process and processes the required information in Microsoft Teams.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: Runs monthly, starting July 1, 2026.
User Data: Gets all users from SharePoint, processes them, and builds a filter.
Time Entries: Retrieves time entries for those users, parses and filters them for today.
Tasks & Projects: Gets tasks and projects, groups them by type (Project, Sprint, Cycle).
Grouping: Projects are grouped, and related tasks are organized.
Variables: Uses array variables to store grouped data.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Scheduled)

1. Trigger
Monthly recurrence. The documented start is 1 July 2026. Each run is the WT process for that cycle.

2. User data
All users are read from SharePoint, processed, and turned into a filter that limits the later time-entry query.

3. Time entries
Time entries for those users are retrieved, parsed, and filtered to today.

4. Tasks and projects
Tasks and projects are retrieved and grouped by type: Project, Sprint, and Cycle.

5. Grouping
Projects are grouped, and the tasks that belong to each project are organized under that group.

6. Variables
Array variables hold the grouped project, sprint, cycle, and task data for the rest of the WT process.

Result
The monthly WT run builds an in-memory grouping of today's time entries under Project, Sprint, and Cycle for the SharePoint user set. The documented steps stop at that grouped data.

Flow Work: Processes meeting attendance and captures attendance duration/time.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: When an item is created or modified in SharePoint, with conditions on attendance and JSON.
Actions:
Parse Attendance JSON (Compose).
Initialize and set attendance variables.
Get Task ID and send HTTP request to SharePoint for task details.
Get all users and initialize ArrayTime.
Loop through attendance array (Apply to each), check conditions, update or create items in SharePoint, and handle additional logic for time entries.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated)

1. Trigger
SharePoint "When an item is created or modified". The trigger conditions require attendance data and valid JSON. Items that fail those conditions do not continue.

2. Parse attendance JSON
A Compose action parses the attendance JSON on the item into a structure the later steps can read.

3. Attendance variables
Attendance variables are initialized and then set from the parsed JSON.

4. Task lookup
The task id is taken from the item. An HTTP request is sent to SharePoint to get that task's details.

5. Users and ArrayTime
All users are retrieved. An array variable named ArrayTime is initialized to collect time values while the attendance rows are processed.

6. Apply to each attendance row
For each element in the attendance array the flow:
- evaluates the row conditions
- updates the existing SharePoint item or creates a new one
- runs the additional time-entry logic for that row

Result
Meeting attendance duration is written onto SharePoint tasks and time entries. This flow does not post the daily attendance report; that report is a separate scheduled flow.

Flow Work: Updates the Assigned To user for the selected task or record.

Trigger: The flow starts manually with a button.
Action 1: Sends an HTTP request to SharePoint to get items assigned to "Umang Kumar" with specific filters.
Action 2: For each item returned, the flow:
Uses a "Compose" action to process the item.
Updates the item in SharePoint using the "Update item" action.

Technical runtime path (Instant / manual button)

1. Trigger
Manual button. There is no SharePoint trigger and no schedule.

2. HTTP request to SharePoint
The flow gets items currently assigned to "Umang Kumar", using the filters configured on that request. Only items that match those filters are returned.

Flow Work: Automatically rearranges or updates time-bucket information according to configured rules.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: Starts when an item or file is modified in your SharePoint site.
User & Task Data: Retrieves users and tasks, filters for specific users, and sorts tasks by priority.
Task Processing: Loops through tasks, gathers time entries, and calculates hours.
Category & Time Entry: For each task, fetches category info, creates time entries, and updates SharePoint lists.
Variables: Uses variables to track totals, arrays, and status throughout the flow.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated)

1. Trigger
SharePoint "When an item or a file is modified" on the site. A modification is the start event for rearranging time buckets.

2. User and task data
Users and tasks are retrieved. The task set is filtered to the specific users in scope, then sorted by priority. Priority order controls the sequence of the later loop.

3. Task processing
The flow loops the sorted tasks, gathers the time entries for each task, and calculates hours.

4. Category and time entry
For each task it fetches the category, creates the time-entry records required by the rearrangement, and updates the SharePoint lists.

5. Variables
Totals, arrays, and status are kept in variables across the loop so each task's hours roll into the running rearrangement.

Result
A SharePoint modification recalculates and rewrites time-bucket entries in priority order for the filtered users.

Flow Work: Processes HHHH users and updates their working-bucket information.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: When an item is created or modified in your SharePoint list, the flow starts.
Variables: Initializes variables for tracking total minutes, increments, and additional details.
Get Changes: Retrieves changes for the item.
Condition: Checks if certain columns have changed and if TaskArrangementMode is true.
User & Category: Gets all users and categories, then processes each user.
Nested Actions: For each user, checks conditions, fetches tasks, processes schedules, updates items, and manages variables.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Automated)

1. Trigger
SharePoint "When an item is created or modified".

2. Variables
Total minutes, an increment variable, and additional details are initialized before any user is processed. These accumulate the working-bucket calculation.

3. Get changes
The flow retrieves the changes on the triggering item so it can see which columns actually changed.

4. Condition gate
The run continues only when the checked columns have changed and TaskArrangementMode is true. If TaskArrangementMode is not true, the working-bucket update does not proceed.

5. Users and categories
All users and all categories are retrieved.

6. Nested per-user actions
For each user the flow checks the user-level conditions, fetches that user's tasks, processes the schedule, updates the SharePoint items, and updates the running variables (minutes, increment, additional details).

Result
HHHH working buckets are recalculated only for a real column change while TaskArrangementMode is on. Each user's tasks and schedule are written back to SharePoint.

Flow Name: Update Assigned to User in Task list
Flow Work: Instantly updates the Assigned To user in the HHHH Task list.
Details Explain working:
Trigger: Manually triggered by a button.
Action 1: Sends an HTTP request to SharePoint to get items filtered by PriorityRank, PercentComplete, and AssignedTo.
Action 2: Uses "Apply to each" to loop through the SharePoint items.
Action 3: Updates each item in SharePoint within the loop.
Technical Working:
Technical runtime path (Instant / manual button)

1. Trigger
Manual button against the HHHH task list.

2. HTTP request to SharePoint
Items are retrieved with filters on:
- PriorityRank
- PercentComplete
- AssignedTo
Only rows that satisfy all three filters enter the loop.

3. Apply to each
